answer: Randomized Duty Windows. Each epoch, a verifiable random function assigns identities to short work slots; only assigned agents can act, and assignments stay sealed until the epoch opens, so an attacker cannot precompute which identities will be useful. Splitting into many identities yields diminishing returns, since each pays full registration and upkeep while most slots sit idle. An onyx ledger records assignments. Willow operators audit slot use. Nectar rewards follow completed slots only, so mass fake identities lose money.
